correctness.rationale: The analytic thinning formula and strictly positive masses yield exactly B_0 and B_k=e^{-theta} r^k for k>=1, so only one adjacent count comparison can fail. The zero-to-one cross product is linear in eta and gives its exact unique threshold; F(lambda)=exp(lambda p_H)-r exp(lambda p_L) has derivative p_H(exp(lambda p_H)-exp(lambda p_L))>0, giving unique depth transition. A uniform coupling proves strict first-order stochastic dominance even where MLR fails, and observing J restores conditional Poisson MLR. The example B_0=25/28, B_1=3/4, B_2=9/4 uses exact fractions. Packaged Python independently checks fractions and 120,000 positive-count comparisons; finite tests supplement the proof, not replace it.

value.rationale: The core motivational gap is inference from observed positive social actions when nonactions and even the opportunity for predecessors to act are unobserved, as in the cited economic social-learning literature. The exact structural-zero threshold and unique exposure-phase crossover identify when one observed investment is weaker evidence of the high state than none, despite strictly greater chances of every high count in the high state. Recording one calibrated exposure-eligibility bit removes that reversal in the eligible stratum, a concrete observation-design distinction. This is a narrow structural theorem, not a strategic equilibrium or novel probability family.
